A Roman scientist said periods could kill bees with a look 🐝

Pliny the Elder wrote in his encyclopedia Natural History (77 AD) that a woman on her period could dim mirrors, kill bees and make fruit fall off trees. None of it is true. A period is the lining of the uterus shedding when an egg isn't fertilized, usually every 24 to 38 days, with about 6 to 8 teaspoons of blood on average.

See a doctor if periods last more than 8 days or suddenly get heavier.

Sources: Pliny's Natural History, Britannica, Mayo Clinic, nidirect, Vagina Museum.
